title: Calibrate two backlash dials to their target setpoints and lock them
context: Precision calibration dials and optomechanical stages on AI hardware test benches exhibit mechanical backlash that requires directional take-up before an indicator accurately tracks adjustment. An autonomous service robot must infer and compensate for backlash hysteresis during calibration routines without human intervention to accelerate experimental and assembly pipelines.
instruction: Adjust both sliding knobs until the white marker lamps on their indicator bars light up, then press the yellow LOCK button beside each rail.
setup: All positions are cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left); the table top is z = 0. Base plate: 32.0 x 44.0 x 1.0 cm dark grey, 5.0 kg, centre (28.0, 0.0, 0.5), friction 1.0, fixed. Two parallel tracks at y = +15.0 (left, orange knob) and y = -15.0 (right, teal knob), each 14.0 cm long from x = 20.0 to 34.0: dark-grey side walls 0.6 cm thick and 2.0 cm tall, 0.5 cm end-stop walls at both ends (inner length 13.0 cm, travel 10.0 cm), inner width 3.6 cm, 0.2 cm floor made of 2.0 cm position bands that alternate light grey and blue from the near stop outward (0-2 blue, 2-4 light, ... 8-10 blue), then grey. Knobs: 3.0 x 3.0 x 1.4 cm, 80 g, friction 0.5, orange (left track, starts at s = 30 mm) and teal (right track, starts at s = 70 mm), resting on the floor with 0.3 cm play per side. LOCK buttons: pocket rings 4.4 x 4.4 x 1.6 cm (0.3 cm walls, dark grey, fixed) centered beside the tracks at (27.0, +7.5) and (27.0, -7.5) holding yellow caps 3.6 x 3.6 x 1.2 cm, 20 g, spring 100 N/m, travel 0.8 cm to a hard stop; cap tops rest 2.4 cm above the plate. Meter housings 4.0 x 12.0 x 2.0 cm dark grey above each rail at x = 38.0 cm (y = +15.0 and -15.0) each carrying a 10-lamp cyan indicator bar (y spans 10.0 cm, 1.0 cm per lamp), a white target marker lamp at the setpoint (Left: 65 mm, Right: 40 mm), and a green locked lamp.
scoring: Setting s of a knob = distance in mm from the near end stop to the knob's rear face; Left starts at 30 mm (setpoint 65 mm), Right starts at 70 mm (setpoint 40 mm). Displayed position = true rail position, except after a direction reversal the display holds still until the knob has moved 6 mm further (then follows with 6 mm lag while moving in that direction). The white marker lamp lights when displayed position is within setpoint +- 2.5 mm. Pressing the yellow LOCK button (travel >= 6.4 mm) latches the dial's currently displayed value; pressing it again unlocks the dial. Score at the end: 0.25 if a knob moved >= 5 mm; 0.50 if one dial is locked in band (displayed value within setpoint +- 2.5 mm); 0.75 if both dials are locked in band; 1.00 if both dials are locked in band, both grippers open, and both knobs still (speed <= 5 mm/s) for 20 consecutive control steps (1.0 s at 20 Hz). Score 0 for the whole run if the base plate moves > 5 mm, a knob leaves its channel (lateral deviation > 1.0 cm or lifted out), more than one lock attempt outside the target band is made on a dial, or a third lock attempt is made on a dial.
reset_notes: Push the orange left knob to 30 mm and the teal right knob to 70 mm (measured from the inner face of each near end stop to the knob's rear face); they rest where left. Check that both yellow button caps spring back to 2.4 cm above the plate, both meter bars reset with no lamps lit, and the base plate has not shifted. Unlock both dials if locked.
fidelity: Knobs slide along U-channels by friction (Coulomb 0.5, no springs). LOCK caps are 100 N/m spring sliders with 8 mm travel, hard stops, and 20 Hz hysteresis. The 10-lamp indicator bars, target marker lamps, locked indicators, and 6 mm backlash deadband/lag logic are computed in code and teleported via write_pose. Real-world build: precision lead-screw or rack calibration sliders with physical backlash, optical linear scales, and LED pushbuttons.
